specification.title: Managed transaction: catch a unique violation, then return normally
steps: Start a transaction with the framework's ordinary callback or context-manager API.
Write the marker `tx` and make sure the write was sent.
Insert the duplicate value 'taken' into uniq. Catch the unique violation at the application layer. Send nothing else.
Checkpoint `before-end`: report the same backend PID. Send no query.
Allow the callback or context manager to finish normally, so the framework uses its ordinary completion path.
Checkpoint `after-api`: report the same backend PID as soon as that API has returned, before any reuse.
On the same pool or connection, run one new transaction that writes the marker `reuse` and commits. Checkpoint `reuse-after-write` if that transaction starts.
Checkpoint `after-end`, as soon as the case function has returned.

invariants.statement: The run recorded the application-visible outcome and an independent database outcome that agree with each other. This invariant does not judge whether the application-visible outcome was the correct commit report. That judgment is in the research summary.

execution.description: Programmatic TransactionTemplate. HikariCP 7.1.0 with maximumPoolSize 1. No other pool setting is changed. Between the two units the connection is released through Spring's normal path. The pool is not closed, the connection is not evicted, and no validation query is issued between them. TX-03 runs only in this mode and in declarative-pooled.

configuration.rollbackRule: TransactionTemplate default: RuntimeException and Error. A checked SQLException is rethrown as SqlUnchecked where the case needs it to leave the callback.

execution.form: TransactionTemplate.execute. The callback catches SQLException and returns.

server.version: PostgreSQL 18.6 (Debian 18.6-1.pgdg13+2) on aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (Debian 14.2.0-19) 14.2.0, 64-bit

fault.mechanism: A unique_violation raised by PostgreSQL inside the transaction, and caught by the application. No statement is withheld or rewritten.
fault.injection_point: After the first write, before the transaction API finishes.
fault.expected_server: The failed statement aborts the transaction unless the application has recovered through a savepoint. This variant does not create a savepoint.
fault.expected_client: The application catches 23505. The framework then finishes the transaction through its ordinary API.

knowledge: The application caught the unique violation. Whether PostgreSQL's later reply is visible depends on the driver and the framework.

api_outcome.basis: TransactionTemplate.execute returned normally, so the template committed
api_outcome.contract: Spring Framework 7.0.9 TransactionTemplate.execute (org.springframework.transaction.support.TransactionTemplate) obtains a transaction, runs the callback, and calls PlatformTransactionManager.commit only when the callback returns. On a RuntimeException or Error it rolls the transaction back and rethrows that same throwable. On any other throwable it rolls back and throws java.lang.reflect.UndeclaredThrowableException. If rollback throws TransactionSystemException, rollbackOnException stores the callback throwable with initApplicationException and throws the TransactionSystemException instead. DataSourceTransactionManager.doCommit calls Connection.commit and translateException wraps a SQLException as TransactionSystemException("JDBC commit failed", ex). Connection.commit is void and does not return a command tag. A normal return from execute is reported as committed. The callback's own throwable leaving execute is reported as rolled_back. Any other throwable leaving execute is reported as failed. Propagation.NESTED, Spring Framework 7.0.9: "Execute within a nested transaction if a current transaction exists, behave like REQUIRED otherwise." Its note says actual nested transactions work on DataSourceTransactionManager. DataSourceTransactionManager's class javadoc says nestedTransactionAllowed defaults to true and nested transactions use JDBC savepoints. Propagation.REQUIRES_NEW: "Create a new transaction, and suspend the current transaction if one exists." No custom rollback rule is installed on the template. TransactionCallback cannot throw a checked SQLException. Where a case needs that error to leave the callback, the callback rethrows it as SqlUnchecked, a RuntimeException, so the template's RuntimeException rule sees it. That wrap is application code. It is not JdbcTemplate's exception translation.

violation.message: ERROR: duplicate key value violates unique constraint "uniq_code_key" Detail: Key (code)=(taken) already exists.

probe.reason: the next transaction is the reuse probe; DriverManagerDataSource closes the connection when Spring releases it
